### 11.1. Construction of the sieve minorant $\mathfrak{m}$

To construct the minorant $\mathfrak{m}$ , we first apply Buchstab’s identity twice (10.3) to get for any $\sqrt{X}<n<X$

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{1}_{\mathbb{P}}(n)=\rho(n,\sqrt{X})=\rho_{0}(n)-\rho_{1}(n)+\rho_{2}(n) $$

where

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{0}(n) \displaystyle:=\rho(n,Z) \displaystyle\rho_{1}(n) \displaystyle:=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\begin{subarray}{c}n=pm\\
Z\leqslant p<\sqrt{X}\end{subarray}\end{subarray}}\rho(m,Z) \displaystyle\rho_{2}(n) \displaystyle:=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\begin{subarray}{c}n=p_{1}p_{2}m\\
Z\leqslant p_{2}<p_{1}<\sqrt{X}\end{subarray}\end{subarray}}\rho(m,p_{2}). $$

For $\rho_{1}$ we first split according to whether $p<U$ to get

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{1}=\rho_{1}^{<U}+\rho_{1}^{\geqslant U}. $$

For the second term we apply Buchstab’s identity (10.3) to the variable $p=k$ with $\mathbf{1}_{\mathbb{P}}(k)=\rho(k,X^{1/4})$ , noting that $U>X^{1/4}$ (so-called role-reversal), to obtain

$$ \displaystyle-\rho_{1}^{\geqslant U}(n)=-\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\begin{subarray}{c}n=pm\\
U\leqslant p<\sqrt{X}\end{subarray}\end{subarray}}\rho(m,Z)=-\rho_{1,0}^{\geqslant U}(n)+\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U}(n) $$

where

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{1,0}^{\geqslant U}(n):= \displaystyle\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\begin{subarray}{c}n=km\\
U\leqslant k<\sqrt{X}\end{subarray}\end{subarray}}\rho(m,Z)\rho(k,Z) \displaystyle\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U}(n):= \displaystyle\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\begin{subarray}{c}n=pkm\\
U\leqslant pk<\sqrt{X}\\
Z\leqslant p<X^{1/4}\end{subarray}\end{subarray}}\rho(m,Z)\rho(k,p). $$

We split the second sum according to whether $p$ lies in the Type II range $[V,W]$ to get

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U}(n)=\underbrace{\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U,<V}(n)}_{p<V}+\underbrace{\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U,[V,W]}(n)}_{p\in[V,W]}+\underbrace{\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U,>W}(n)}_{p>W}. $$

In

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U,>W}(n)=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\begin{subarray}{c}n=pkm\\
U\leqslant pk<\sqrt{X}\\
W<p<X^{1/4}\end{subarray}\end{subarray}}\rho(m,Z)\rho(k,p). $$

we may apply Buchstab’s identity (10.3) to $\rho(m,Z)$ (in the reverse direction) to extract a prime factor $Z\leqslant q<W$ , to get

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U,>W}(n)=\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U,>W,[Z,V)}(n)+\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U,>W,[V,W]}(n)+\rho_{1,1,1}^{\geqslant U,>W}(n), $$

where

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U,>W,[Z,V)}(n):=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\begin{subarray}{c}n=pkqm\\
U\leqslant pk<\sqrt{X}\\
W<p<X^{1/4}\\
Z\leqslant q<V\end{subarray}\end{subarray}}\rho(m,q)\rho(k,p), \displaystyle\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U,>W,[V,W]}(n):=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\begin{subarray}{c}n=pkqm\\
U\leqslant pk<\sqrt{X}\\
W<p<X^{1/4}\\
\max\{V,Z\}\leqslant q<W\end{subarray}\end{subarray}}\rho(m,q)\rho(k,p), \displaystyle\rho_{1,1,1}^{\geqslant U,>W}(n):=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\begin{subarray}{c}n=pkm\\
U\leqslant pk<\sqrt{X}\\
W<p<X^{1/4}\end{subarray}\end{subarray}}\rho(m,W)\rho(k,p). $$

Similarly, for the term $\rho_{2}(n)$ we split the sum according to whether $p_{2}$ lies in the type II range $[V,W]$ to get

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{2}=\rho_{2}^{<V}+\rho_{2}^{[V,W]}+\rho_{2}^{>W}. $$

Combining the above, we have for $\sqrt{X}<n<X$

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{1}_{\mathbb{P}}(n)=\mathfrak{m}(n)+\mathfrak{d}(n), $$

where the minorant is defined by

$$ \displaystyle\mathfrak{m}:=\rho_{0}-\rho_{1}^{<U}-\rho_{1,0}^{\geqslant U}+\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U,[V,W]}+\rho_{1,1}^{\geqslant U,>W,[V,W]}+\rho_{2}^{[V,W]} $$

where we write

$$ \omega_{y,z}(n):=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\begin{subarray}{c}p\mid n\\
y\leqslant p<z\end{subarray}\end{subarray}}1. $$

The error term from $\mathbf{1}_{p^{2}\mid n}$ is negligible by (9.4) with $z_{0}=y=X^{\nu+\eta}$ . We begin by removing the “main term” contribution. By Siegel Walfisz and the large sieve (to bound the $r\leqslant(\log X)^{10A}$ contribution and the $(\log X)^{10A}<r\leqslant R$ contribution respectively, where $r$ is as in the definition of $b_{n}^{(\gamma)}$ from §2.2), we have that

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\end{subarray}}\mu(n)b_{n}^{(\gamma)}\ll_{A}\frac{HX^{1/2}}{\log^{A}X}. $$

Applying Halász to deal with the contribution of small moduli $r\ll(\log X)^{1/100}$ and the large sieve for larger moduli yields that

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\begin{subarray}{c}n\\
p|n\implies p\not\in[y,z)\end{subarray}\end{subarray}}\mu(n)b_{n}^{(\gamma)}\ll\nu HX^{1/2}(\log X)^{-1/1000}. $$

It follows that

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\end{subarray}}\mu(n)a_{n}^{(\gamma)}=-\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\begin{subarray}{c}m,p\\
y\leqslant p<z\\
(m,p)=1\end{subarray}\end{subarray}}\beta_{m}w_{mp}^{(\gamma)}+O_{A}\biggl(\nu HX^{1/2}+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}h<H\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n^{2}+h\ll X\end{subarray}}\mathbf{1}_{p|n^{2}+h\implies p\not\in[y,z)}\biggr), $$

where we take

$$ \beta_{m}:=\frac{\mu(m)}{1+\omega_{y,z}(m)}. $$

With $y=X^{\nu+\eta}$ and $z=X^{1/20}$ , we remove the terms $p\mid m$ by (9.4) and then apply Proposition 2.4 to obtain

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}\begin{subarray}{c}m,p\\
y\leqslant p<z\\
(m,p)=1\end{subarray}\end{subarray}}\beta_{m}w_{mp}^{(\gamma)}\prec\mathrel{\mkern-5.0mu}\prec\frac{HX^{1/2}}{R^{1/4}}. $$

An upper bound sieve applied to the sum over $h$ yields that

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}h<H\end{subarray}}\mathbf{1}_{p|n^{2}+h\implies p\not\in[y,z)}\ll H\prod_{\begin{subarray}{c}y\leqslant p<z\end{subarray}}\biggl(1-\frac{1}{p}\biggr)\asymp\nu H. $$

Thus,

$$ \sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}h<H\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n^{2}+h\leqslant X\end{subarray}}\mathbf{1}_{p|n^{2}+h\implies p\not\in[y,z)}\ll\nu HX^{1/2}. $$

The desired result follows upon collecting (12.1), (12.2), (12.3), and (12.4). For $H=X^{1/2-o(1)}$ , fix $\nu_{0}>0$ , take $\eta<\nu_{0}/100$ and $y=X^{\nu_{0}+\eta}$ , and run the proof uniformly for $X^{1/2-\nu_{0}}\leqslant H\leqslant X^{1/2}$ . This gives $O(\nu_{0}HX^{1/2})$ ; now let $\nu_{0}\to 0$ .
